sections.title: Performance Analysis — Job Dashboard
sections.content: This is a Python/SQLite job-scraping and matching pipeline (no React frontend exists in this repo — `find . -iname "*.tsx" -o -iname "*.jsx"` returns nothing — so I've substituted the closest equivalents in Python: redundant recomputation and un-batched I/O).

sections.title: 1. N+1 query / write pattern (the biggest issue) — `ingest.py` + `db.py`
sections.content:
`run_ingest` loops over every scraped job and calls `insert_job`, which does **one SELECT + one INSERT + one `commit()` per row**:

```python

sections.title: db.py
sections.content:
def insert_job(conn, job: JobListing):
    ...
    if job_exists(conn, job.job_url):      # SELECT #1
        return False
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO jobs ...")   # INSERT
    conn.commit()                          # fsync to disk, every single row
    return True
```

For N scraped jobs that's 2N round trips and N fsyncs. `upsert_company` has the identical shape (SELECT existence check + `commit()` per row). At a few hundred jobs per run this is seconds of pure I/O wait that should be milliseconds.

**Fix** — batch the existence check and defer commits to one transaction per source:

```python

sections.title: db.py
sections.content:
def insert_jobs_bulk(conn, jobs):
    urls = [j.job_url for j in jobs if j.job_url]
    existing = set()
    if urls:
        placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(urls))
        existing = {row[0] for row in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT job_url FROM jobs WHERE job_url IN ({placeholders})", urls
        )}
    inserted = 0
    for job in jobs:
        if job.job_url in existing or not _valid(job):
            continue
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO jobs (...) VALUES (...)", (...))
        existing.add(job.job_url)   # guards dupes within the same batch too
        inserted += 1
    conn.commit()   # one fsync for the whole batch
    return inserted
```

`upsert_company` should follow `upsert_embed_score`'s existing pattern — a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE` — which removes the SELECT entirely:

```python
def upsert_company(conn, company: Company):
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO companies (name, funding_amount, funding_round, sector, hq,
             founders, source, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
           ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE SET
             funding_amount=excluded.funding_amount, funding_round=excluded.funding_round,
             sector=excluded.sector, hq=excluded.hq, founders=excluded.founders,
             last_seen_at=excluded.last_seen_at""",
        (company.name, company.funding_amount, company.funding_round, company.sector,
         company.hq, company.founders, company.source, now, now),
    )
```

Then in `ingest.py`, commit once per source batch instead of once per row, and dedupe within a batch before hitting the DB at all (two sources can legitimately return the same `job_url`).

sections.title: 2. Missing indexes → full table scans as the DB grows
sections.content:
`duplicate_of` (added via `ALTER TABLE`, no index) is filtered on in three separate query functions:

```python

sections.title: jobs_needing_embed_score, top_unranked_jobs, canonical_jobs_for_dedup
sections.content:
WHERE j.duplicate_of IS NULL
```

Every one of these does a full table scan today. Add a partial index in `init_db`:

```python
conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_jobs_active ON jobs(duplicate_of) WHERE duplicate_of IS NULL")
```

sections.title: 3. SQLite tuning for bulk writes
sections.content:
No pragmas are set anywhere — default `journal_mode` (rollback journal) + per-row `commit()` is the worst-case combination for write throughput. In `init_db`:

```python
def init_db(path):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
    ...
```

Combined with batched commits from #1, this alone should take bulk ingest from O(N) fsyncs to O(1).

sections.title: 4. Caching opportunity — `profile_text.py`
sections.content:
`compose_profile_text()` re-reads and re-hashes the profile/evaluation files from disk on every call. It's currently only called once per pipeline run (fine today), but if a future scoring loop calls it per-job, that's a redundant disk read + SHA-256 hash every iteration. Worth memoizing at the call site (or `functools.lru_cache` on a version keyed by file mtime) once it's wired into a per-job loop — flagging now so it's not missed later:

```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def compose_profile_text(profile_file=PROFILE_FILE, evaluation_file=EVALUATION_FILE):
    ...
```

sections.title: 5. Resource handling — `db.py`
sections.content:
`init_db` returns a raw `sqlite3.Connection` that's never closed via a context manager anywhere in the codebase (checked `src/` and `tests/`). Not a leak Python's GC won't eventually clean up, but under `pytest` running many tests each opening its own SQLite file, unclosed connections can exhaust file descriptors on a large suite. Prefer:

```python
with sqlite3.connect(path) as conn:
    ...
```
or ensure callers explicitly `conn.close()` when a pipeline run finishes.

sections.title: 6. Minor — `jobspy_source.py`
sections.content:
`df.iterrows()` is the slowest way to walk a pandas DataFrame (row-by-row Python object construction). At `results_wanted=20` default it's irrelevant, but if that's ever raised into the hundreds/thousands, switch to `df.itertuples()` or vectorized `.to_dict("records")` — itertuples is ~10x faster for this access pattern.

---

**Priority order:** #1 (batched writes + `ON CONFLICT` upsert) and #3 (WAL + deferred commit) together are the real win — they turn ingest from O(N) synchronous disk fsyncs into effectively one write. #2 matters once the `jobs` table has thousands of rows. #4–6 are small, worth doing opportunistically but not urgent.
